title.narrative: IOM: Förebyggande av könsbaserat våld, fas 2
IOM: Prevention of gender-based violence 2nd phase

description.narrative:
IOM i Colombia har inkommit med ett förslag till den Svenska Ambassaden i Bogota om stöd för implementeringen av projektet ”Prevention of gender-based violence – second phase”, med 14 440 000 SEK under en treårsperiod.
Det huvudsakliga målet med insatsen är att bidra till implementeringen av fredsavtalet och till före detta kvinnliga Farc-kombattanters ökade politiska, sociala och ekonomiska egenmakt i sin återintegreringsprocess till civila livet. Insatsen inkluderar två specifika områden: 1) förebyggande av könsbaserat våld, och 2) främjande av kvinnors politiska, sociala och ekonomiska autonomi. Detta skall uppnås genom följande resultat: 1)En strategi för förebyggandet av könsbaserat våld implementerat i åtta regioner med deltagandet av 300 kvinnor och men (före detta kombattanter och medlemmar av samhällena) och 100 tjänstemän. 2)Åtta initiativ för ekonomisk egenmakt implementerat med ett jämställdhetsperspektiv. 3)Tre förskolor designade och fungerande som gynnar 90 barn, med deltagandet av 50 kvinnor och män i utvecklandet av handlingsplaner och kapacitetsutvecklande processer i dessa förskolor.

The objective of this project support is to contribute to the implementation of the Peace Accord and to the political, social, and economic empowerment of former female combatants from FARC in their reincorporation process to civil life. The intervention includes two specific areas: The prevention of gender-based violence and the promotion of women's political, social, and economic autonomy. This is to be achieved through a strategy for the prevention of gender-based violence; nine economic empowerment initiatives; and three care-centres. This project is the second phase, building upon the previous contribution with ID-number: 11004.

The main objective of the intervention is to contribute to the implementation of the Peace Accord and to the political, social and economic empowerment of former female combatants from FARC in their reincorporation process to civil life.
Two specific areas are proposed: 1) Prevention of gender based violence and 2) Promotion of women, political, social and economic autonomy. It is expected that at the end of the project the following results will be achieved:
1) A strategy for the prevention of gender-based violence implemented in eight regions with the participation of 300 women and men (former combatants and members of the communities) impacting 100 public servants.
2) Eight economic empowerment initiatives implemented with a gender perspective, with an impact in the communities.
3) Three Care Centers designed and functioning benefitting 90 children. 50 women and men participate in the elaboration of action plans and capacity building processes for these Care Centers.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
Some of the results achieved by the project are:
Output 1: Prevention of Gender-based violence Strategy:
Eight Gender-based violence (GBV) prevention plans were designed and implemented through a participatory process, in eight prioritized regions: Tierra Grata (Cesar), Caño Indio (Norte de Santander), La Montañita (Caquetá), Vista Hermosa (Meta), La Carmelita (Huila), Mutatá (Antioquia), Pereira (Risaralda), and Popayán (Cauca). 3.339 persons (60% women and 40% men) participated in the elaboration of the plans, surpassing the initially planned target of 300 persons. This included women and men in reincorporation processes and members of the communities.
The Prevention plans were reinforced through 696 activities which included workshops, communication strategies, sport events, cinema forums, meetings with local entities, and meetings with target groups. These activities were also used as a strategy to inform on the causes of gender-based violence (GBV), on the different types of violence, as well as to identify risk factors and to learn about different assistance processes for the attention of cases of gender-based violence in each region.
52 women and men strengthened their leadership capacities through a course on Prevention of GBV in the following thematic areas: peace building, prevention of GBV, youth and peace, and sexual and reproductive rights.
Several products were developed throughout the implementation of the project which are an important tool for the continuation of activities to prevent and assist cases of GBV with the communities, with the local governmental entities, and other local institutions.
Some of these products are:
Booklets: "Mi cuerpo es mío" (It is my body); "Nos cuidamos" (We take care of one another); Selfprotection with a gender perspective.
"New Masculinities for Peace" (MazPaz) - this booklet was developed with the support of the international organization "Promundo" and is a tool to promote new masculinities. It was used in workshops, and in different recreational activities with the communities to promote gender equality and to contribute to transform current gender norms in the eight territories.
Output 2: Economic Empowerment Initiatives
Nine (9) economic initiatives were designed and implemented with the participation of 127 women and 27 men. Their capacities in administrative, productive and organizational issues were strengthened through training in these areas. This figure is lower than the target initially established of 300 women and men. The main reasons for this is that the initiatives are still in a consolidation process even though the project has finished. Additionally, the participation of beneficiaries was also affected by the deterioration of the security conditions that forced the displacement of the persons from some of the Transitional Spaces for Training and Reincorporation (ETCRs) to other regions of the country.
The economic initiatives were selected through a broad process, taking into consideration the local context, the capacity of the women participating in the initiatives, the resources within the regions, and their commercial potential and sustainability. Technical assistance was provided to the participants through Universidad Nacional, and a local assessment on the context was made for each region, as an input for the business plans.
IOM implemented different actions - such as coordination with national and local governmental entities, with civil society organizations, the private sector and other projects funded by the international community - to promote and strengthen the initiatives, to become collective productive projects that could contribute to the generation of income for women former combatants, and to their economic empowerment. However, in this process, security risks, as well as economic, organizational and political factors affected the initiatives in different ways in each of the eight regions.
The aim with the initiatives was to contribute to the economic empowerment and economic autonomy of women in reincorporation processes. Nevertheless, only 26% of women and men beneficiaries perceived an increase in their economic autonomy (target 60%).
Despite the challenges faced, at the end of the project the nine initiatives have a business plan, which include: the organizational structure, the production, commercialization and financial plans. Five of the nine initiatives have reached a permanent operation; three have had a discontinuous operation and one initiative is not active due to the displacement of the persons from the ETCR in Vista Hermosa, Meta.
Output 3: Community Care Centers
Three care centers were designed and implemented in the regions of: Tierra Grata (Cesar), La Montañita (Caquetá) and Popayán (Cauca). These regions were selected based on an analysis of the possibilities within the ETCRs, which included the security conditions, possible synergies with the local entities, and infrastructure. 114 women and men participated in the design and implementation of the Care Centers (target 50 women and men), who strengthened their capacities on child rights, youth, environmental care, and food soveirignty, through courses implemented within the project.
411 boys and girls (target 90 boys and girls) participated in the different activities provided by the Care centers, which included: environmental care awareness among children, support in school homeworks, promotion of healthy habits, cultural and sport activities, among others.
The child care center at Tierra Grata will continue to operate through the contractor hired by the Instituto de Bienestar Familiar (Family Welfare governmental entity). Coordination efforts were carried out with the local institutions to continue providing support to afterschool homeworks, and agreements were reached with the community to provide volunteers for these activities.
The care center at La Montañita will continue as a support to the cultural groups and community needs. The material and assets of the project were donated to the care center. Environmental care activities will continue under the coordination of one of VIVAS "promotoras" (leader).
The care center in Popayán will continue activities under the financial support of "Las Manuelitas" organization, and will provide care services and activities during holidays.
At the end of the project, the care centers are an alternative for child care in the three regions, contributing to release women from child care activities and to have more time to participate in different political, organizational and economic activities.
